No. The evidence shows tree-cover loss on about 81.3 ha in 2021, which is roughly 2.2% of the 3,643.5 ha property, so most of it was not affected. A further 37.3 ha of loss came in patches under 0.5 ha, which the method doesn't count as events.

The loss is corroborated. A later year in the series was observed, and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the affected area. The national forest map puts about 68.1 ha of it in planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), 13.2 ha outside mapped forest, and none in native forest.

"Cleared" would claim more than the data shows. Tree-cover loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation. The evidence does not establish deforestation or land-use change, the cause, legality, who was responsible, or any compliance finding.
